How We Cut Build Times in Half

Posted by the Platform team

BLOG_BODY_MARKER Our continuous integration pipeline had grown slow and flaky over three years of steady feature work. A clean build took close to twenty minutes, and engineers were context switching away from their work while they waited. We decided to treat build speed as a first-class reliability problem and gave a small team a quarter to fix it.

The first win came from caching. We introduced a remote build cache keyed on the content hash of every compilation input, so unchanged modules were never rebuilt. That alone removed roughly a third of the wall-clock time on a typical pull request, and it made repeated builds on the same branch nearly instant.

The second win came from parallelism. We restructured the dependency graph so that independent modules could compile concurrently across a pool of workers. Combined with the cache, the median build dropped from nineteen minutes to just under nine. Flaky integration tests were quarantined and rewritten one by one until the suite was trustworthy again.

The lesson, for us, was that build speed is a product. Treating it with the same rigor we apply to user-facing latency paid for itself within a single quarter, and the team has guarded those numbers ever since.
